entries.root_cause: Monitoring-source row creation was coupled to a privileged AFTER INSERT bootstrap that granted volatile host-inventory runtime admission. Logical restore, relocation, COPY, or replay can legitimately recreate source rows through INSERT, so object existence incorrectly became sufficient evidence of current recovery and placement authority.
horizontal_audit: monitoring source creation versus runtime admission
future provider source bootstrap side effects

entries.root_cause: The host-inventory resource projection protected state and poll-authority fields but omitted provider-derived observation timestamps from the guarded mutation set. A same-tenant direct writer could therefore forge freshness or regress durable observation chronology without accepted provider evidence.

The runtime-admission table was made UNLOGGED to fail closed across physical recovery, but logical backup semantics were not separately governed. PostgreSQL logical dumps include unlogged-table rows by default, so stale placement and recovery admission could cross a dump/restore boundary and regain current polling authority without successor-epoch re-admission.
horizontal_audit: physical recovery versus logical recovery semantics
all ephemeral authority state that must not cross logical copies

entries.root_cause: Host-inventory conformance was split across migration-era harnesses, allowing green evidence from historical schemas to be interpreted as assurance for the composed exact-head schema. Later executor, recovery-epoch and projection-authority migrations could therefore regress previously proven behavior without those scenarios being replayed against the schema actually shipped.
horizontal_audit: logical recovery and authority projection guards

entries.root_cause: Host-inventory operation authority was guarded only on UPDATE. Because the modeled tenant runtime can INSERT monitoring_sync_operation rows, it could manufacture an operation already in running/claimed state with the source's current poll epoch and generation, bypassing the guarded claim transition and reusing current-state authority.
horizontal_audit: public completion entry points that trust claimed-operation rows

entries.root_cause: Completion fenced stale poll generations before evidence insertion but did not fence the outer recovery/placement poll epoch. After recovery advanced the source epoch while preserving local poll generation, an old running operation could reach the snapshot epoch trigger, raise, roll back the completion transaction, and remain permanently running under obsolete authority.
horizontal_audit: completion ordering of outer epoch versus inner generation fences
recovery successor-epoch transitions with in-flight work

entries.root_cause: The application worker returned the provider-read result computed before persistence, even though the database completion path can authoritatively supersede or reject that result and persist reconciliation_required. Application-visible outcome therefore diverged from the durable operation truth.
horizontal_audit: application return values after persistence fences
worker results after stale generation or epoch retirement
API/BFF status projection from durable operations

entries.root_cause: The broad final-schema conformance remained pinned through migration 016 even after migration 017 replaced the complete host-inventory function. A narrow 001-to-017 recovery test covered only the superseded-epoch branch, leaving normal success, removal, ordering and logical-recovery behaviors tested against a schema that was no longer the exact shipped schema.
horizontal_audit: exact-head migration composition in broad conformance
success and removal paths after final hardening
future migration additions after final-schema harness creation

entries.root_cause: Claim-time authority froze poll epoch/generation but left the operation's monitoring_source_id, source_instance_generation, configuration_revision and scope_revision mutable while running. A same-tenant writer could therefore rewrite an in-flight provider read onto newer source/revision authority before completion, defeating stale-authority checks that trusted the claimed operation row.
horizontal_audit: all claim-snapshotted ownership and revision fields

entries.root_cause: Host Inventory enqueue, claim and completion were SECURITY DEFINER functions owned by the guarded executor but remained executable by PUBLIC. That collapsed the runtime specialization boundary: an unrelated same-tenant runtime could invoke the privileged provider-integration path directly, choose claim/completion inputs, and obtain executor-backed evidence mutation without being the authorized provider worker.
horizontal_audit: all SECURITY DEFINER Monitoring worker entrypoints
runtime.worker specialization to database capability binding

entries.root_cause: Operation authority was frozen only after claim, while direct DML could still create lifecycle-clean pending Host Inventory work or rewrite the pending source/generation/configuration/scope tuple. A later legitimate claim validated the adulterated tuple as current and thereby converted attacker-shaped work into authoritative provider execution.
horizontal_audit: Host Inventory enqueue versus direct INSERT
alternate DML command paths around protected functions
future metric/problem ingestion operation creation and claim lifecycles
